children: Eight to 10 lenders are expected to participate in the 10-year facility, with SBI likely to take about Rs 7,000 crore exposure

Vodafone Idea (Vi) is putting together a consortium of eight to 10 lenders for a Rs 35,000-crore, 10-year term loan as the telecom operator prepares to raise funds for capital expenditure over the next decade, according to people familiar with the matter.

State Bank of India (SBI) has approved a proposal to take about 20 per cent of the exposure, or around Rs 7,000 crore. The remaining loan is expected to be divided among other public and private sector lenders, with a minimum exposure of Rs 1,500 crore per lender, the people said.

“SBI has done an internal assessment which came to about Rs 35,000 crore of loans needed. Now it is up to the company to get other lenders on board. The company will totally need Rs 60,000 crore to upgrade its services, which means some of it will have come from internal accruals or equity infusion later,” said a person familiar with the details.

SBI has set certain conditions for the proposed loan. Any shortfall in investment above the loan amount during the period will have to be managed by Vodafone Idea, according to people familiar with the matter.
Kumar Mangalam Birla, who returned as chairman of Vodafone Idea in May 2026, will also have to remain chairman for the tenure of the loan, the people said.

“SBI would have an oversight over the cash flows of the company and all funds will be routed to their accounts. There is also a clause that the Aditya Birla Group has to maintain its equity stake in the company after converting its warrants and rights. There is also a comfort guarantee from a group company which is part of the conditions,” said a second person aware of the details.

The Aditya Birla Group and associated companies currently own about 6.64 per cent of Vodafone Idea, making them the third-largest shareholder after the Government of India and UK-based Vodafone, which holds about 19 per cent. The government owns about 49 per cent of the telecom operator after converting certain dues into equity.
Bankers are seeking assurances from the group that Vodafone Idea and its creditors will have continued support if the company's plans do not progress as expected, according to the people.

“Kumar Birla had earlier quit the Vi board in 2021 when the company was burdened by high government outgoes and falling revenues. He came back as chairman in May this year as things improved. Banks want to make sure that they are not left in a lurch if things do not work out,” the second person said.
Vodafone Idea did not respond to an email seeking comment.

The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) is expected to be the second-largest lender in the consortium, with an exposure of about Rs 4,000 crore. NaBFID did not respond to an email seeking comment.

Punjab National Bank, Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and Union Bank of India are also in discussions with Vodafone Idea and are likely to join the consortium, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Large private sector lenders including ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank are also in discussions with the company. The contours of the loan are expected to be finalised by the middle of October, the person said.
